root_cause: The autoComplete library's default keydown handler for the Escape key clears the input value when dismissing the suggestion list, instead of preserving the user's typed input.
repair_strategy: Add a custom keydown event handler in the autoComplete configuration that intercepts the Escape key, prevents the default behavior (which clears the input), and programmatically closes the suggestion list while preserving the input value.

edits.before: events: { input: { selection: event => { window.cityPicker.input.value = event.detail.selection.value; } } }

expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Escape while editing a city will dismiss the autocomplete suggestions without losing the user's typed input, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order) by ensuring keyboard dismissal works predictably.
functional_risks: If the library's event system replaces rather than chains keydown handlers, arrow key navigation may break (mitigated by only handling Escape and not calling preventDefault for other keys)
The close() method may not exist on the instance (guarded with typeof check)
verification_requirements: ArrowDown and Enter still select suggestions
Form submission saves the typed city
